items.title: Agentic engineering with GitLab and your local agent: A walkthrough
items.summary: You can build an agentic engineering environment to drive greater automation throughout your workflow. How? Start in the harness you already use and connect to GitLab Duo Agent Platform once with a skill. Longer, repository-aware workflows run on GitLab, and every merge request still hits the same reviews, pipelines, scans, and approval policies.In this article, we will show you how to quickly get started, from setup to tackling four key use cases. We focus on Claude Code as the local harness because that’s what we see most of our customers using but this same flow can apply to the local harness of your choosing, including Duo CLI.How to configure your agentic engineering environmentIf you already do most of your coding in a local harness, keep working there and wire it to GitLab Duo Agent Platform. From the terminal, you can direct lifecycle work to agentic workflows that run inside GitLab:Picking up an issue and opening a merge requestReviewing every MR as it landsResolving merge conflictsRepairing a pipeline that just failedWith GitLab Ultimate, triaging and fixing security findings once code landsClaude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and others become the place from where you direct that work.Part 1 is the setupInstall the GitLab Duo setup skill, ask Claude Code to run it, and it sets up your whole top-level group with the necessary settings, the flows, an automation in every project, and the MCP connection.Part 2 walks through four workflowsYou can try them as soon as the setup is done, each driven from Claude Code:Find an issue assigned to you and hand it to the Developer flow.Get automated code reviews on your merge requests, act on the findings without leaving your harness, and resolve any conflicts that pop up.Use an automation to fix a failed pipeline.On Ultimate, triage and fix security findings with the security flows.When you want an even tighter loopThe MR followup skill guides your local harness through the steps above even faster. The skill helps local agents monitor progress on the repo-side and take actions on your behalf to speed things along.What you need before you startA GitLab.com top-level group with GitLab Credits (Premium and Ultimate groups get access to promotional free credits each month for each user). The security workflow in Use Case 4 requires Ultimate licensing for your GitLab instance.A project in that group with a pipeline, a few open issues, and an open merge request or two, so the workflows have something to act on.The Owner role on the top-level group, so the skill can set up the whole group. If you're a Maintainer on the project but not a group owner, the skill sets up just that project and lists what to ask your Owner.Claude Code installed and signed in, plus git and the GitLab CLI (glab, signed in with glab auth login ), which the skill uses to read and change settings.Part 1: Guided setup with a skillThe GitLab Duo setup skill accelerates the connection from inside your harness. You install the skill once, ask Claude Code to set up GitLab Duo. The skill sets up your group as it turns on group-wide Duo Agent Platform workflows, creates the Fix CI/CD Pipeline automation where needed, connects to GitLab MCP server, and reports anything left for you to finish.Install the skillgit clone https://gitlab.com/gitlab-da/projects/agentic-eng-config.gitcp -R agentic-eng-config/skills/gitlab-duo-setup ~/.claude/skills/cp -R agentic-eng-config/skills/gitlab-mr-followup ~/.claude/skills/Then Claude Code picks it up in the running session. If it isn't listed, restart Claude Code. You can add the skill to .claude/skills/ inside the repo so teammates can use it too.Run the skillIn your project directory, start Claude Code and invoke the skill with a slash command:/gitlab-duo-setupNote: Different harnesses can have a different syntax for invoking skills.What happensBefore it changes anything, the skill reads your top-level group and its projects and shows you one plan: every change and what it covers (the groups or projects). Group changes reach every downstream project and every member, and the plan says so. It waits for your yes, and you can drop any line. Then it:Turns on GitLab Duo Agent Platform and flow execution for the group, and adds the Code Review, Duo Developer, and Fix CI/CD Pipeline flows to the group's flows. Flows you already have stay on.Turns on automatic code review for the group, which carries down to every project.Creates an automation in every project with CI/CD that runs Fix CI/CD Pipeline when a pipeline fails. Projects that already have one are skipped, so running the skill twice is safe.Adds the GitLab MCP server to Claude Code, user-level or project-level as you prefer, and walks you through signing in in the browser.Verifies by calling list_duo_agents_and_flows.
